title: PWM 调速：电机电流跟着占空比走
summary: 把 5.4 的 MOSFET 低边开关换成 PWM 来开关：线圈把电流抹平，电机只“看见”平均值。测不同占空比下的平均电流、续流二极管里的电流，再比较 1 kHz 和 20 kHz。
concepts: PWM 调速 PWM speed control
低边 MOSFET 开关 low-side MOSFET switch
平均值与有效值 average and RMS
PWM 频率选择 PWM frequency choice
description: ESP32 的 PWM 引脚 → 100 Ω → IRLZ44N 栅极（10 kΩ 下拉）；MOSFET 低边开关一个由独立 5 V 稳压电源供电的电机，电机两端反并联续流二极管。电机线圈把电流抹平，平均电流跟着占空比走；MOSFET 关断时电流经二极管续流。比较 25 / 50 / 100 % 占空比，以及 1 kHz 和 20 kHz。

cards.title: 占空比调到多低，电机还转？
text: 搭回 5.4 的低边开关：引脚 → **`100 Ω`** → **IRLZ44N** 的栅极，栅极再接 **`10 kΩ`** 到 GND；**5 V 稳压电源** → 电机 → 漏极，源极接 GND；**续流二极管**并在电机两端，色环朝 5 V。稳压电源的 − 接开发板 GND。
这次把引脚设成 **PWM**，**`20 kHz`**、**`50 %`**。电机转起来了。
在「属性」里把占空比降到 **`25 %`**。电机还转吗？MOSFET 每次照样把整整 5 V 接上又断开——到底什么变了？

cards.title: 线圈把电流抹平
text: - 电机里有一个线圈。线圈的电流不能突变：它像一个沉重的飞轮，推一下、松一下，转速只是慢慢变。
- 20 kHz 时开关每 50 µs 一次，比线圈“反应”快得多，电流几乎是一条直线，停在**平均值**。1 kHz 时周期变长，电流来得及涨落，成了锯齿。
![](fig:current)
- MOSFET 断开的那一段，线圈还要维持电流。电流改走**续流二极管**，绕电机一圈回来；没有它，漏极会冲出很高的电压。
![](fig:freewheel)
- 所以电机只“看见”平均电压 D × 5 V，平均电流就是它除以电机的 8 Ω：
$$\bar I_M ≈ \frac{D × 5}{8}$$
- 代入 D = 80 %：$\bar I_M ≈ \frac{0.8 × 5}{8} = 0.5$ A。续流时二极管的压降也落在电机上，所以实际还要小一点；占空比越低，这一点越显眼。

cards.title: 测平均电流和续流电流
text: - 占空比调回 **`50 %`**，点**「检查我的电路」**。检查会自己换占空比（25 / 50 / 100 %）和频率（1 kHz）。
- 电流表**串在电机支路**里，直流档读到的就是**平均值**。二极管的电流可以单击二极管在「属性」里看。
- 最后一题换成 **`1 kHz`**，用电流表的**真有效值（RMS）**档。先预测，再读。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **PWM 调的是平均值**：线圈把电流抹平，转速跟着平均电流走，不跟峰值走。
- **低占空比有死区**：电机要一定的电流才能克服静摩擦（这里的模型是 0.1 A），不够就只会嗡嗡响。
- **电机用 ≥ 20 kHz**：1 kHz 时电流锯齿状涨落，平均差不多，有效值却更大——线圈更热，还能听见啸叫。LED 没有线圈，≥ 1 kHz 就不闪。
- 真实电路里的坑：续流二极管用快速或肖特基的（1N5819），1N4007 在 20 kHz 下太慢；电机电源和开发板**共地**；别用 GPIO0 / 2 / 5 / 12 / 15 驱动栅极——它们上电时会抖一下，电机跟着抽一下。

caption.text: 同样 50 % 占空比：20 kHz 时电机电流几乎是一条直线；1 kHz 时成了锯齿。平均值差不多，锯齿的有效值更大。

i18n.en: The same 50 % duty: at 20 kHz the motor current is almost a straight line; at 1 kHz it is a sawtooth. The averages are about the same; the sawtooth has the larger RMS.

caption.text: Q1 断开时：线圈维持电流 I_M，电流经 D1 绕回电机（续流）。Q1 闭合时 D1 反偏，不导通。

i18n.en: Q1 off: the coil keeps I_M flowing, and it returns round the motor through D1 (freewheeling). With Q1 on, D1 is reversed and carries nothing.

en.title: PWM speed control: the motor current follows the duty cycle
en.summary: Drive the low-side MOSFET switch from 5.4 with PWM: the coil smooths the current, so the motor only "sees" the average. Measure the average current at several duty cycles and the current in the flyback diode, then compare 1 kHz with 20 kHz.
en.description: An ESP32 PWM pin → 100 Ω → the IRLZ44N's gate (10 kΩ pull-down); the MOSFET switches the low side of a motor powered by a separate 5 V bench supply, with a flyback diode across the motor. The motor's coil smooths the current, so the average current follows the duty cycle; while the MOSFET is off the current freewheels through the diode. Compare 25 / 50 / 100 % duty, and 1 kHz with 20 kHz.
compare: - **25 %**: pin average 0.82 V; motor average 0.71 V, **89 mA**, of which 66 mA (75 %) flows in the diode. 89 mA is below the model's 0.1 A start current — **the motor doesn't turn**. Real motors have this dead band too: static friction needs a minimum current, and a low duty just hums.
- **50 %**: average 2.06 V, **258 mA**, 129 mA in the diode (it freewheels half the time); the RMS is also 258 mA — almost no ripple (the 50 µs period is ≪ τ).
- **100 %**: the MOSFET stays on (Vgs = 3.26 V, ohmic region, Rds ≈ 44 mΩ), the motor takes **620 mA** and the diode is idle.
- The average current is not exactly ∝ duty: during freewheeling the diode's drop (about 0.85 V at this current) also appears across the motor, and at low duty that part weighs more.
- At turn-off the drain only reaches **5.7 V** (the diode clamps it to 5 V plus one diode drop). Without D1 it would fly up to the IRLZ44N's 55 V avalanche voltage.

- **1 kHz, 50 %**: the 1 ms period is 4 τ, so the current decays a lot while off. The average (263 mA) is about the same as at 20 kHz, but the **RMS is 317 mA** — winding heat ∝ I_rms², about 45 % more — and 1 kHz is right where the ear is most sensitive: the motor whines.

measurements.ask: 20 kHz, 25 %: the motor's average current (DMM on DC amps in series with the motor)
measurements.explain: The motor averages only about 0.71 V, ≈ 89 mA, below the model's 0.1 A starting current: it hums but does not turn.
≈ 258 mA. The average is not strictly ∝ duty: the diode's drop is also across the motor while freewheeling.

measurements.ask: Same state: the average current in the flyback diode D1
measurements.explain: During the half of each period the MOSFET is off, the motor current flows back through D1 to +5 V: ≈ 129 mA.

measurements.ask: From your two readings, the fraction of the motor current that goes through the diode, I_D1 / I_M1
measurements.explain: ≈ 0.5 = 1 − D: the 50 µs period at 20 kHz ≪ τ = L/R, so the current barely changes; it just flows through the MOSFET half the time and through D1 the other half.

measurements.ask: Now 1 kHz, 50 %: the RMS motor current (true-RMS range)
measurements.explain: A 1 ms period is 4τ, so the current sags a lot while off: the average (263 mA) is about the same, but RMS ≈ 317 mA and winding heat ∝ I_rms² rises by about 45%; 1 kHz also whines audibly. Motors use ≥ 20 kHz.

hints: Gate: PWM pin → 100 Ω → G, plus 10 kΩ from G to GND. S to GND, D to the motor's − end.
The diode's band (cathode) faces the motor's 5 V end, its anode goes to the drain: while the MOSFET is on, it is reversed.
The bench supply's − must be connected to the board's GND.
Set the PWM pin to 20 kHz.
tests: 20 kHz, 25 %: too little average current, the motor does not start
20 kHz, 50 %: motor runs, RMS ≈ average, part of the current freewheels through the diode
20 kHz, 100 %: MOSFET fully on (ohmic), diode off
1 kHz, 50 %: about the same average but a larger RMS (hotter, audible whine)
Output LOW: MOSFET off, motor stopped

cards.title: How low can the duty go before the motor stops?
text: Rebuild the low-side switch from 5.4: pin → **`100 Ω`** → the **IRLZ44N**'s gate, plus **`10 kΩ`** from the gate to GND; **5 V bench supply** → motor → drain, source to GND; a **flyback diode** across the motor, band towards 5 V. Connect the supply's − to the board's GND.
This time set the pin to **PWM**, **`20 kHz`**, **`50 %`**. The motor turns.
In **Properties**, lower the duty to **`25 %`**. Does the motor still turn? The MOSFET still connects and disconnects the full 5 V every time — so what changed?

cards.title: The coil smooths the current
text: - A motor contains a coil. A coil's current cannot jump: like a heavy flywheel, push and release and its speed only changes slowly.

- At 20 kHz the switch flips every 50 µs, much faster than the coil can react, so the current is almost a straight line at the **average**. At 1 kHz the period is longer, the current has time to rise and fall, and it becomes a sawtooth.
![](fig:current)
- While the MOSFET is off, the coil still pushes its current on. It goes through the **flyback diode** and round the motor; without the diode the drain would shoot up to a very high voltage.
![](fig:freewheel)
- So the motor only "sees" the average voltage, D × 5 V, and the average current is that divided by the motor's 8 Ω:
$$\bar I_M ≈ \frac{D × 5}{8}$$
- With D = 80 %: $\bar I_M ≈ \frac{0.8 × 5}{8} = 0.5$ A. While freewheeling, the diode's drop also sits across the motor, so the real value is a little lower — more noticeably at low duty.

cards.title: Measure the average and the freewheeling current
text: - Set the duty back to **`50 %`** and press **Check my circuit**. The check changes the duty (25 / 50 / 100 %) and the frequency (1 kHz) by itself.
- Put the ammeter **in series with the motor**: on DC it reads the **average**. For the diode's current, click the diode and look in Properties.
- For the last question switch to **`1 kHz`** and use the ammeter's **true RMS** range. Predict first, then read.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **PWM sets the average**: the coil smooths the current, and the speed follows the average current, not the peak.
- **Low duty has a dead zone**: a motor needs some current to overcome static friction (0.1 A in this model); below that it only hums.

- **Use ≥ 20 kHz for motors**: at 1 kHz the current saws up and down — about the same average but a larger RMS, so a hotter coil and an audible whine. LEDs have no coil; ≥ 1 kHz is enough to stop flicker.

- Real-world catches: use a fast or Schottky flyback diode (1N5819) — a 1N4007 is too slow at 20 kHz; give the motor supply and the board a **common GND**; don't drive the gate from GPIO0 / 2 / 5 / 12 / 15 — they twitch at power-up and so does the motor.

tests.name: 20 kHz、25 %：平均电流太小，电机转不起来
20 kHz、50 %：电机转，RMS ≈ 平均，一部分电流走续流二极管
20 kHz、100 %：MOSFET 完全导通（可变电阻区），二极管不导通
1 kHz、50 %：平均差不多，但 RMS 更大（更热、能听见啸叫）
输出低电平：MOSFET 截止，电机停

compare: - **25 %**：引脚平均 0.82 V；电机平均 0.71 V、**89 mA**，其中 66 mA（75 %）在续流二极管里；89 mA 低于模型的 0.1 A 起转电流——**电机转不起来**。真实电机也有“死区”：静摩擦要靠一定的电流才能克服，低占空比只会嗡嗡响。
- **50 %**：平均 2.06 V、**258 mA**，二极管里 129 mA（一半时间在续流）；RMS 也是 258 mA——电流几乎没有纹波（50 µs 的周期 ≪ τ）。
- **100 %**：MOSFET 一直导通（Vgs = 3.26 V，在可变电阻区，Rds ≈ 44 mΩ），电机 **620 mA**，二极管不导通。
- 平均电流不是严格 ∝ 占空比：续流期间二极管的压降（这个电流下约 0.85 V）也落在电机上，低占空比时这部分比例更大。
- 关断瞬间漏极只到 **5.7 V**（二极管把它钳在 5 V 再加一个二极管压降）。把 D1 拿掉，漏极会冲到 IRLZ44N 的 55 V 雪崩电压。
- **1 kHz、50 %**：周期 1 ms 是 τ 的 4 倍，关断期间电流衰减很多。平均电流 263 mA 和 20 kHz 差不多，但 **RMS 317 mA**——线圈发热 ∝ I_rms²，多了约 45 %；而且 1 kHz 正好在人耳最敏感的频段，电机会“吱吱”叫。

measurements.ask: 20 kHz、25 %：电机的平均电流（万用表直流档串在电机支路里）
measurements.explain: 电机平均只有约 0.71 V，≈ 89 mA，低于模型的 0.1 A 起转电流：转不起来，只会嗡嗡响。
≈ 258 mA。平均电流不严格 ∝ 占空比：续流时二极管的压降也落在电机上。

measurements.ask: 同一状态：续流二极管 D1 的平均电流
measurements.explain: MOSFET 关断的那一半时间里，电机电流全部经 D1 流回 +5 V：≈ 129 mA。

measurements.ask: 用你的两个读数算电机电流里走二极管的比例 I_D1 / I_M1
measurements.explain: ≈ 0.5 = 1 − D：20 kHz 的周期 50 µs ≪ τ = L/R，电流几乎不变，只是一半时间走 MOSFET、一半时间走 D1。

measurements.ask: 改成 1 kHz、50 %：电机电流的有效值（真有效值档）
measurements.explain: 周期 1 ms 是 τ 的 4 倍，关断时电流衰减很多：平均 263 mA 差不多，但 RMS ≈ 317 mA，线圈发热 ∝ I_rms²，多约 45%；而且 1 kHz 能听见啸叫。电机用 ≥ 20 kHz。

hints: 栅极：PWM 引脚 → 100 Ω → G，G 再接 10 kΩ 到 GND。S 接 GND，D 接电机的 − 端。
二极管的色环（阴极）朝电机的 5 V 端，阳极接漏极：MOSFET 导通时它是反着的。
稳压电源的 − 必须和开发板的 GND 接在一起。
